abstract: Innate immune responses shape Muller glia (MG) reprogramming and retinal regeneration, yet the contribution of individual immune cell type remains poorly defined. Neutrophils enter the blood-retinal-barrier (BRB)-damaged retina within hours of injury, but their role in retinal regeneration is unknown. Here we report that neutrophils are required for the regenerative responses in needle-poked, but not NMDA-injured, zebrafish retinas. Pharmacological ablation of neutrophils with Erbb2 inhibitors suppresses MG proliferation, progenitor formation, and subsequent neuronal regeneration after stab injury, whereas neutrophil depletion has no significant effect in the BRB-intact NMDA model. We further show that Cxcl12-Cxcr4b signaling retains neutrophils at the stab injury site, and manipulating neutrophil retention correspondingly alters the regenerative responses. Mechanistically, neutrophils may modulate MG reprogramming and proliferation by regulating microglial reactivity and by secreting a regeneration-promoting factor Hb-egf. These data identify neutrophil as a previously unrecognized regulator of retinal regeneration and establish that their contribution is injury context-dependent.
